motion_evidence.angle_convention: Screen coordinates, positive clockwise; cyan opposite-pair axis unwrapped modulo 180 degrees by dense temporal continuity. Approximate measured angles, not individual same-color sail identity.
motion_evidence.initial_acceleration: First 0.5s averages 25.81 deg/s; 0.5–1.0s averages 61.43 deg/s. Subsequent complete half-second intervals remain approximately 60.6–62.3 deg/s, so this is an initial ramp followed by near-constant speed, not sustained acceleration.
motion_evidence.ending: Final 0.125s averages about 31.8 deg/s; end eases down without reversing.
motion_evidence.symmetry_caveat: Opposing cyan sails and opposing yellow sails repeat appearance every 180 degrees. Sparse start/end poses cannot identify revolutions; temporal unwrapping uses all 124 frames and is corroborated by every-three-frame visual progression. No 1.5-turn claim: measured travel is about 0.81 turn; turn count is not a user gate.

frame_evidence.finding: Cyan axis progresses about 44.7, 57.6, 88.3, 118.9, 149.2 degrees: slow start followed by clockwise advance.
Unwrapped cyan axis continues about 180.1, 210.6, 241.1, 271.6, 302.0, 333.2, 337.2 degrees. No return arc or reversal.

Upper cyan sail black outer tip outline reaches y=0 and has slight boundary clipping; top row has 5,10,14,15,13,16 dark pixels respectively. Cyan fill remains below the boundary: this is small outline clipping, not loss of a large blade section.

Four connected sails remain readable, with cyan and yellow opposite pairs; no duplication, gross bending or detached sails. Cream tower, red roof, blue door/cyan window, purple shutters, fence, flowers and green hill remain recognizable and intact. No added faces. Mild generative shape/scale drift is visible; exact geometric rigidity is not asserted.

acceptance_criteria.criteria_distinction: Tiny outline-only boundary contact is assessed for visible impact rather than automatically failing overall acceptance. Strict framing compliance still fails, and its original review is preserved unchanged.

visual_acceptability_assessment.reason: The four colored sails remain readable and connected throughout the chronological samples. Rotation progresses coherently without rocking, gross deformation, duplication, or lost colored blade area. The bright tower, garden and flowers remain intact. Tight framing is noticeable when examining the early vertical pose, but the small outer-outline contact does not read as a missing sail or an abrupt visual disruption and is not substantial enough to spoil the reward animation.
visual_acceptability_assessment.framing_caveat: Frames 20–25 occupy six frame durations, approximately 0.25s at 24 fps. Only a small black outer-tip outline meets/is slightly clipped at the top border; no cyan fill is lost. This is a real minor defect retained in the review, not a claim of perfect framing.
visual_acceptability_assessment.reinspection: Reopened all three chronological contact sheets, native-resolution top-edge strips for frames 16–27, and full native-resolution frame 24 with view_image. Reused the existing all-frame angular measurements and exact-hash evidence.
visual_acceptability_assessment.limitation: Judgment is based on decoded chronological frame inspection and angular tracking, not real-time video playback or a child usability study.
